title: Business Breakfast | Stock/Share Market News | 20th August 2026 || TV5 Money

recommendations.note: Sugar sector highly cyclical, changes every 2-3 months. Stock rose from Rs 36 (Jul 30) to near 50. Chance of further move to 60. Keep doing partial profit booking.
recommendations.detail: Caller bought 3,000 shares at Rs 50. Kutumba Rao said: 'Sugar sector is highly cyclical. I did not think a continuous one-way rally would come, but for the next six months it looks safe. On July 30, Dwarakesh was at Rs 36, now near 50. There is a chance of some more upward move up to 60. Keep doing partial profit booking.'

recommendations.note: Textile pick for festival season. Larger stocks like Arvind can hold ground when rally fizzles. Not a wealth-creation sector -- on-and-off returns.
recommendations.detail: Caller asked for two textile stocks for festival season. Kutumba Rao said: 'I will recommend Arvind. Smaller stocks like KG Denim or Trident fizzle out fast. Whereas Welspun or Arvind can hold their ground. Not a wealth-creation sector -- gives on-and-off returns tied to trade deals and news.'

recommendations.note: Second textile pick alongside Arvind for festival season momentum.
recommendations.detail: Kutumba Rao recommended SP Apparels as the second textile stock alongside Arvind for the caller asking about festival season plays.

recommendations.note: Stay invested. All three CDMO companies (Laurus, Divi's, Shilpa Medicare) on same platform. If additional funds, put in Shilpa Medicare.
recommendations.detail: Caller at 250% profit wanted to shift to Divi's or Shilpa Medicare. Kutumba Rao said: 'All three are on the same platform in CDMO. Stay invested in Laurus. If there are additional funds, put them in Shilpa Medicare.'

recommendations.note: CDMO beneficiary. Recommended for deploying additional funds alongside Laurus Labs position.
recommendations.detail: Kutumba Rao said: 'If there are additional funds, I would say put them in Shilpa Medicare.' Recommended as additional CDMO exposure alongside Laurus Labs.

recommendations.note: Stock corrected from 400+ to ~355. Raw materials problems for 2 quarters. Patience needed. Exit when it returns to 400+.
recommendations.detail: Caller fed up with SMS Pharma (bought at Rs 143). Kutumba Rao said: 'Hold even SMS. Stock corrected from 400-plus to around 355. If he wants to exit, exit and switch when it comes back to 400-plus. Raw materials problems for two quarters due to gestation crisis. Another quarter may also face difficulty.'

recommendations.note: Book partial profits. Rose unexpectedly from 170-180 to 325 (52-week highs). June results in line but not great.
recommendations.detail: Caller at 100% profit. Kutumba Rao said: 'Marksans has risen unexpectedly from 170-180 to 325. Book partial profits if already holding. Wait for correction before fresh buying. June results in line but not great.'

recommendations.note: Entire solar pack underperforming badly. Hype around KP group is over. Better to exit on rallies.
recommendations.detail: Caller at 25% loss. Kutumba Rao said: 'The entire solar pack is underperforming badly. KP Energy even more so. There was a lot of hype around the entire KP group at one time, and now everything has gone to sleep. Better to come out during rallies.'

recommendations.note: Near 52-week low. Company stood its ground. Institutional selling almost exhausted. Only a matter of time. Technically very weak.
recommendations.detail: Caller bought at Rs 79. Kutumba Rao said: 'Hold. Even though dark clouds were placed over it, the company has stood its ground. Institutional equity selling must exhaust -- they say it has almost exhausted. Only a matter of time. But technically, Suzlon looks very weak.'

recommendations.note: Near 52-week low (315). Bought at 389, price will come back. Lighten position a bit at 360, but do it ex-dividend.
recommendations.detail: Caller bought at Rs 389. Kutumba Rao said: 'Hold. Trading in narrow band, 52-week low at 315. He bought at lower price, not at 400-plus, so price will come back easily. Lighten position a bit if it comes to 360, but do it ex-dividend.'
